guide.about: IDSW is a community-led developer conference run by PERKODI with Indonesian tech communities (Python ID, id-ruby, TEKNUM, JakartaJS, Deeptech.id). The 2026 edition runs 21-22 November at Usmar Ismail Hall, Jakarta Selatan. Venue tickets are sold out per the site FAQ; streaming tickets are sold via TipTip and there is a stream site at stream.idsw.dev.

sections.title: Reading the agenda (our interpretation)
bullets: Agentic AI dominates: both days open with an agentic-AI keynote, plus talks on agentic coding in a regulated financial company, the first 100 days of AI coding assistants at a large bank, an analytics agent meeting real warehouse data, and a lightning talk on keeping secrets out of LLM agents.
LLM systems: a keynote on inference engineering, the inner workings of fast LLM serving.
AI-adjacent craft: building a browser engine with AI, design engineering after the front-end-is-dying claim, human attention, and mentorship for junior engineers.
Classic engineering: zero-trust networking as a dependency, how voice travels between devices as packets, and one organization-failure talk.
The through-line for a builder of AI-assisted software: agents meet reality - measured speed claims, production failures, serving costs, secret handling, and verification.

sections.title: Day 1 priorities (our suggestion)
bullets: 09:45 Robin's keynote: agentic workflows on local LLMs. Listen for model sizes, hardware assumptions, and where they still fall back to cloud.
11:10 Thomas's talk: whether agentic coding actually made a regulated team faster. Listen for how they measured - metrics, review load, incident rates - not just the conclusion.
13:30 Mustafa's keynote: inference serving internals. Reusable when weighing self-hosted models against APIs: batching, latency, cost per token.
16:30 Faiq's talk: what broke when an LLM agent met real BigQuery data. Failure modes worth turning into tests.

sections.title: Day 2 priorities (our suggestion)
bullets: 10:05 Mansur's keynote: from AI prototype to safe, tested, trustworthy production. Compare the verification mindset with how we mark proof boundaries in releases (synthetic tests vs device-confirmed behavior).
13:55 Kresna's talk: building a browser engine with AI - where AI assistance stops helping on a large, specification-heavy codebase.
14:30 Lightning block: especially the SOPS talk on secret handling for LLM agents and the build-vs-subscribe-vs-on-premise talk.
16:30 Eko's closing keynote: topic not yet announced at check time.

sections.title: Questions worth carrying (ours)
bullets: For the local-LLM keynote: what minimum hardware makes an agentic local LLM practical today, and what still forces a cloud fallback?
For the regulated-industry talk: which agent-written code still needs human sign-off, and how is that enforced in tooling?
For the analytics-agent talk: what was the first production failure, and how was it detected?
For the SOPS lightning talk: what is the threat model - an agent reading the repository, or an agent with tool access to a secret store?
